title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sits in the 'Cristaux' notes. The surrounding typed pages are a draft of SGA4-style base change (exposé XII/XVI, Lemme 8.4), and the handwriting is unrelated to them. It is Grothendieck's scratch work on encoding an F–V structure (Dieudonné module, crystal, or truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level 1) by distinguished triangles.

Top: a module (or crystal) M with Verschiebung V: M → M^(p) and Frobenius F. A commutative square relates F, V, F^(p), V^(p) and their Frobenius twists, with the composite V^(p)F noted.

Main construction: an object 𝔛 with F_𝔛: 𝔛^p → 𝔛 and V_𝔛: 𝔛 → 𝔛^p. The two rows at the bottom right make the meaning clear: '𝔛^p – B – 𝔛' says B is the image of F, i.e. F factors through B. '𝔛 – A – 𝔛^(p)' says A is the image of V. For a BT_1 Dieudonné module, Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F, which gives two short exact sequences:
- (I) A → 𝔛^p → B, written as the triangle B →∂_I A →i_I 𝔛^p →π_I B, with ∂_I of degree 1.
- (II) B → 𝔛 → A, written as A →∂_II B →i_II 𝔛 →π_II A.
- (II^(p)) is the Frobenius twist of (II).

The first box recovers the operators as composites through the middle terms:
- F_𝔛 = i_II ∘ π_I : 𝔛^p → B → 𝔛.
- V_𝔛 = i_I ∘ π_II : 𝔛 → A → 𝔛^p.

The second box asks:
- whether the Yoneda composites ∂_I∂_II : A → A[2] and ∂_II∂_I : B → B[2] vanish ('nul?');
- for the induced V_A : A → A^(p), namely π_II^(p) i_I : A → 𝔛^p → A^p;
- for the induced F_B : B^p → B, namely π_I i_II^(p).

Thus A and B inherit F–V structures of their own; this is the recursive structure behind Kraft–Oort 'canonical filtrations' of BT_1.

Second attempt (lower case a, b, X): Grothendieck tries to axiomatise the data abstractly. He takes a triangle II: b →∂_0 a →i_0 X →π_0 b and Frobenius-type pullbacks φ*, ε*. He asks that φ*(II) ≅ (I) and ε*(I) ≅ II^(p), i.e. 'triangles compatibles avec F-V structure'. F and V should then be recovered as F_b = π_0 ε*(i_II) and V_a = ε*(π_II) i_0, both marked '?'.

The sketches '0 – M → M^p – 0', 'M^p – M – 0' encode the periodic exactness M^(p) →F M →V M^(p) →F M. In modern terms the data are an object with two filtrations (images of F and of V), plus Frobenius-semilinear identifications between graded pieces, formulated in a triangulated (derived) way.
errors: In the second box the composite giving V_A is transcribed 'π_II^(p) ∂_I'. This does not type-check; the intended composite must be π_II^(p) ∘ i_I : A → 𝔛^p → A^p.
In the first box, 'π_I ? : 𝔛^p → 𝔛 (F_𝔛)' is incomplete. The correct composite is i_II ∘ π_I.
The lower-case axiomatisation (φ*, ε*, the triangles in a, b, X) is not internally settled: Grothendieck's own question marks remain, and the roles of φ and ε are not defined on the page.
The questions whether ∂_I∂_II and ∂_II∂_I vanish are left open. In general Yoneda composites of two extension classes need not vanish without further hypotheses.

ideas.what: Recovering F and V of a BT_1 / mod-p Dieudonné module as composites through Im F and Im V, using Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F
ideas.modern_name: Structure of BT_1 Dieudonné modules; F-zips (two filtrations with Frobenius-linear identification of graded pieces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kraft (1975, unpublished), Oort (2001, Ekedahl–Oort strata), Moonen–Wedhorn (F-zips, 2004)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74) treat BT_1 and Dieudonné crystals, but not in this triangle form as far as known

ideas.what: Encoding the F–V structure by two distinguished triangles related by Frobenius pullback ('triangles compatibles avec F-V structure'), with induced F, V on the pieces A, B
ideas.modern_name: Derived/triangulated version of F-zips; cf. Frobenius gauges
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moonen–Wedhorn (F-zips); derived analogues later (Fontaine–Jannsen, Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie F-gauges)

ideas.what: Commutative square relating F, V and their Frobenius twists; composite V^(p)F
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius/Verschiebung relations FV = VF = p and their twists

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1970, encodes the F–V structure of a BT_1-type object by two exact triangles: image of V → 𝔛^p → image of F, and image of F → 𝔛 → image of V. Frobenius pullback exchanges them, and the induced F, V on the pieces form a recursive structure. This is essentially the F-zip / Ekedahl–Oort formalism (Kraft 1975, Oort 2001, Moonen–Wedhorn 2004), but phrased triangulatedly.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, apparently unrecorded instance of the F-zip idea in Grothendieck's hand. The triangulated phrasing points toward derived F-zips and F-gauges, a topic developed only much later.

missed.claim: The page leaves open whether the Yoneda composites of the two extension classes vanish, and how to axiomatise the abstract triple (a, b, X) with Frobenius pullbacks.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are exactly the conditions one needs in a derived/triangulated definition of an F-zip-like structure. The fragment, however, is too rough to constitute a result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a rough scratch page showing Grothendieck working out the two-filtration/F-zip-like structure of BT_1 objects in triangle language, years before Kraft, Oort and Moonen–Wedhorn. It is historically interesting, but incomplete and rough, and the underlying facts (Ker F = Im V, etc.) are standard.
transcription_corrections: 'π_I ? : 𝔛^p → 𝔛' should read i_II π_I : 𝔛^p → 𝔛 (F_𝔛).
'π_II^(p) ∂_I : A → A^(p)' should probably read π_II^(p) i_I.
The script letter 𝔛 is a Gothic/script X distinct from the lower-section X. The superscripts '^p' and '^{(p)}' are used interchangeably for the Frobenius twist.
'A^{*2}' / 'B^{*2}' likely denote shifted objects (A[2], B[2]) or Frobenius-twisted ones; the reading is uncertain.
Margin note right: 'triangles compatibles avec F-V structure'.
